sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2024. An overview of the Bantoid languages. Afrika und Übersee 97: 1-46. Hamburg University Press. DOI 10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.288.
sources.note: Nothing about Eman. Bantoid-wide remarks only: sect. 4.2.6 'Bantu is reconstructed as having two tones.. many languages, especially in Zone A, have a more elaborate system, which resembles more closely the three and four-tone systems which are common in Bantoid. Table 8 compiles a sample of descriptions of tone systems for Bantoid and Bantu, only listing languages with three tones or more.' Table 8's Tivoid rows are Ugarə (H, L, U, D; Cassetta & Cassetta 1994b) and Esimbi [Tivoid ?] (H, M, L, R, F; Koenig, Coleman & Coleman 2007). No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the article. No Eman…

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. The Tivoid languages: overview and comparative wordlist. Circulation draft, paper to accompany a presentation at Bantu VI, Helsinki, 20-23 June 2016. Cambridge: McDonald Institute. 20 pp. (Glottolog ref 78922)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any Tivoid language. Eman appears only in Table 1 (800 speakers, source ALCAM), the untoned 120-item ALCAM datasheet column 'Eman [=Amanavil]' in Table 8, and the Central Tivoid B subgrouping (sect. 6.1). Sect. 3.1: 'For Tivoid languages, phonologies of any sort exist for only five languages, Tiv, Iyive, Iceve, Esimbi and Ugarə.' Sect. 3.3 Tones covers only Tiv, Ugarə, Esimbi.
sources.venue: Circulation draft, paper to accompany a presentation at Bantu VI, Helsinki

sources.citation: Starr, Alan & Clark Regnier. 2008 [survey 1990]. Tivoid Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-022. Dallas: SIL International. 52 pp.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey only: sect. 1.1 identifies ALCAM 898 Eman = Amanavil; sect. 3 'Ipulo-Eman-Caka' gives lexicostatistics (Amayo, Amanavil) and RTT intelligibility. No phonology, no stress or tone statement.

sources.citation: Chumbow, S. Beban, Gratien G. Atindogbe, Engelbert Domche & Dieudonne Martin Luther Bot. 2007. Classification of the languages of Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea on the basis of lexicostatistics and mutual intelligibility. African Study Monographs 28(4): 181-204. Kyoto University.
sources.note: Nothing. Eman occurs twice: in the table of intelligibility studies, Wide Bantu clusters, row 'Tivoid: Iceve, Mesaka, Caka, Evand, Ipulo, Eman: Separate languages, confirmed by Regnier (1991).' and in the appendix inventory 'Tivoid (12).. 6. Ipulo [2] 7. Eman [2] 8. Caka [2]'. No language data; the words tone, tonal, stress, accent do not occur in the paper.

Stub: 'Eman is a Tivoid language of Cameroon. The rather divergent dialects are Eman proper and Amanavil.' No phonology.

sources.citation: Tuinstra, Anneke. 2015. Ipulo phonology sketch / orthography (SIL Cameroon, Yaoundé), cited in Blench 2016 as Tuinstra (2015a).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Ipulo is Eman's closest relative (Central Tivoid B, ~50% shared cognates); a phonology of Ipulo is the nearest description of the subgroup and might mention Amanavil/Amayo. Not a description of Eman itself.
